title: The Gravity of the Rust Belt Anew
premise: Ansel Brightwater is a clone of a murdered detective, carrying the original's unsolved case in his inherited memories while hauling cargo through contested orbits to stay invisible. When he intercepts a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct for two centuries, he realizes it's addressed to him by name—and that the sender knows how the original died. Racing a decaying relay reactor's countdown at the edge of dead space, Ansel discovers the signal comes from another clone of himself, one who solved the murder and paid for it. To survive, Ansel must choose between destroying the evidence that could clear his original's name or broadcasting the truth and ending his own anonymity forever; he broadcasts it, finding belonging not in hiding but in being known.
about_author: Astrid Thornbury is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining remote transmission relays before turning to fiction. Their work explores what survives when memory is copied and identity is treated as cargo.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits establishes his careful invisibility: forged manifests, no questions, no history. A customs officer lingers on his genetic profile just long enough to unsettle him. Emotional beat: the exhausting cost of erasure, and the first crack in his belief that invisibility equals safety.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback woven into a sleepless night shift. He reviews the fragmentary memories he inherited from the original Brightwater: a murder case half-solved, a name the original whispered before dying. Emotional beat: grief for a man whose face he wears, resentment at inheriting an enemy he never chose.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. His ship's array catches a repeating transmission in Pre-Collapse Standard—a language extinct two centuries—embedded in static near dead space. Decryption software flags one word rendered in modern script: BRIGHTWATER. Emotional beat: cold dread curdling into compulsion; someone is calling him home.

chapters.title: Manifests and Lies
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He tries to sell the signal's coordinates to a broker and finds every buyer suddenly uninterested—or frightened. One broker warns him that others have asked about transmissions from that sector before disappearing. Emotional beat: paranoia taking root; the invisible life has walls he never built.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV introduces Vess Okonkwo, a linguist stowaway who decoded part of the signal independently and begs passage. She recognizes the dialect as liturgical, meant for a single listener. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Ansel's solitude breached by someone who sees through him too easily.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Militia patrol craft board the freighter hunting a 'genetic echo' matching a five-year-old warrant. Vess hides Ansel's biometric tag inside her translation equipment. Emotional beat: loyalty forming under pressure; Vess chooses him without knowing why, and it terrifies them both.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Under Vess's questioning, inherited memories surface fully: the original discovered clones were being manufactured as disposable witnesses to erase corporate crimes—including his own murder. Emotional beat: horror reframed as purpose; the case was never cold, only buried alive.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They reach the boundary of dead space where the ancient relay hangs, reactor failing, countdown visible on its hull like a wound. The signal source is inside. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo at the threshold; no more running, only forward.

chapters.title: Boarding the Ghost
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. They dock with the derelict relay station; corridors are scrawled with the extinct language, freshly maintained. Someone has lived here recently. Emotional beat: uncanny intimacy—the station feels prepared for them, which is worse than abandonment.

chapters.title: Countdown Doctrine
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They find the reactor's countdown isn't decay—it's deliberate, a dead-man switch tied to a broadcast buffer. When it hits zero, everything stored here transmits to every colony in range. Emotional beat: dawning scale; this isn't a message, it's a verdict awaiting delivery.

chapters.title: The Other Brightwater
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In the station's heart they meet Sable Brightwater—a third clone, older, who cracked the murder case years ago and has been guarding the evidence here ever since. Emotional beat: mirror-shock; Ansel confronts the self he might have become, hardened and alone.

chapters.title: Three Faces of One Man
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Tensions fracture the trio: Sable wants the broadcast, Ansel fears exposure will get everyone killed, Vess demands the truth over both their heads. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh—three people arguing over one soul's obligations.

chapters.title: Evidence of a Murder
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sable shows him the archive: the original's final recordings naming his killer, a director of the cloning consortium itself. Watching them, Ansel experiences the death as if his own. Emotional beat: violation transformed into resolve; the memory becomes his own to carry.

chapters.title: Hunters Arrive
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Consortium retrieval ships exit transit at the relay's edge, drawn by the same signal. Sable reveals she sent it deliberately—as bait. Emotional beat: betrayal and understanding entwined; Sable needed a second clone because a witness requires corroboration.

chapters.title: The Reactor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The countdown accelerates as hunters dock; Sable explains the choice: purge the archive and live hidden forever, or let it broadcast and die as evidence. Emotional beat: the blurb's central race crystallized—minutes left, lives weighed against truth.

chapters.title: Corridors of Static
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Hunters breach the station; Vess uses the liturgical language's acoustics to misdirect them through the relay's resonant corridors. Emotional beat: competence as love; Vess fights not for a cause but for two stubborn men who share one face.

chapters.title: Sable's Confession
chapters.summary: Sable's POV (first departure). She admits she didn't just guard the evidence—she tampered with it, editing recordings out of fear, and the signal was her penance. Emotional beat: guilt laid bare; even the truth-keeper corrupted the truth, and only confession can repair it.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. With hunters closing, Ansel reaches the broadcast core as the countdown enters its final minute. He must physically authorize transmission with his biometrics—making himself the signature on the evidence. Emotional beat: climax of identity; signing the truth means surrendering invisibility permanently.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He authorizes the full, untampered archive—including Sable's corrections—as the reactor vents and hunters flood the chamber. The transmission tears outward toward every colony. Emotional beat: catharsis; the whisper held for five years finally spoken at maximum volume.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Free Fall
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The station breaks apart; the three escape in the freighter as consortium ships scramble, their warrant now worthless against public revelation. Sable, wounded, asks why Ansel trusted the broadcast. Emotional beat: exhaustion and fragile joy; survival as a shared act rather than a private one.

chapters.title: Known Quantities
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Weeks later, colonies debate the broadcast; some call Ansel a hero, others a weapon. He stops forging manifests. Vess stays aboard; Sable recovers, teaching Vess the dead language. Emotional beat: belonging chosen rather than defaulted; visibility as a daily practice.

chapters.title: The Gravity That Holds
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, final chapter. A new signal arrives—in the living tongue this time, from strangers who heard the broadcast and want to help finish the case. Ansel answers openly, first time signing his real name. Emotional beat: resolution; gravity redefined as the pull between people who choose to be found.
